terms.definition: Network Address Translation — replaces a private IP address with a public one for outbound internet communication, then reverses the translation for the reply
terms.example: Like a company receptionist making calls on behalf of employees — the outside world only sees the receptionist's number

terms.definition: A fully managed AWS service that provides NAT for private subnet instances, auto-scaling up to 45 Gbps with no maintenance required
terms.example: Your private EC2 downloads OS patches through NAT Gateway without exposing its private IP

terms.definition: A self-managed EC2 instance configured to perform Network Address Translation, used as a legacy alternative to NAT Gateway
terms.example: An EC2 instance in a public subnet with Source/Destination Check disabled, routing traffic for private instances

terms.definition: A subnet with no route to the Internet Gateway, making its resources unreachable from the internet
terms.example: Your database server lives in a private subnet — it has no public IP and cannot receive inbound internet traffic

terms.definition: A subnet with a route to the Internet Gateway, allowing resources to send and receive internet traffic
terms.example: Your web server lives in a public subnet with an Elastic IP — it can serve web traffic

terms.definition: An EC2 feature that drops any traffic where the instance is neither the source nor destination — must be disabled for NAT Instances
terms.example: Disabling this on a NAT Instance allows it to forward packets meant for other EC2 instances

terms.definition: A static public IPv4 address allocated to your AWS account that you can assign to EC2 instances or NAT Gateways
terms.example: NAT Gateway requires one Elastic IP to serve as its public-facing IP address

terms.definition: An encrypted IPSec tunnel connecting your on-premises network to an AWS VPC over the public internet
terms.example: A company connects its headquarters to its AWS VPC so employees can access cloud resources securely

terms.definition: The AWS-side endpoint of a Site-to-Site VPN connection, attached to your VPC
terms.example: Think of VGW as the door on the AWS side of the VPN tunnel

terms.definition: An AWS resource representing your on-premises router or firewall — the customer-side endpoint of a VPN connection
terms.example: You create a CGW in the console and enter the public IP of your office router

terms.definition: Internet Protocol Security — a suite of protocols for encrypting and authenticating IP network communications
terms.example: AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses IPSec to encrypt all data traveling through the VPN tunnel

terms.definition: A dedicated private physical fiber connection from your on-premises data center to AWS, bypassing the public internet entirely
terms.example: A bank uses Direct Connect to transfer financial data to AWS with consistent low latency and no internet exposure

terms.definition: A colocation facility (third-party data center) where AWS has equipment and where your fiber cable terminates to connect to the AWS network
terms.example: Major cities have Direct Connect locations where customers can arrange physical connections to AWS

terms.definition: A logical connection on top of a Direct Connect physical connection — Private VIF for VPC access, Public VIF for AWS public services
terms.example: A Private VIF routes traffic from your on-premises network directly into your VPC

terms.definition: An AWS network transit hub that connects multiple VPCs and on-premises networks through a single central gateway
terms.example: Instead of peering 10 VPCs with each other (45 connections), connect all 10 to a Transit Gateway (10 connections)

terms.definition: An IT architecture that uses both on-premises infrastructure and cloud resources together as a unified environment
terms.example: A company runs its legacy Oracle database on-premises but runs its web application on AWS, connected via Direct Connect

terms.definition: A dynamic routing protocol used in VPN and Direct Connect connections to automatically exchange routing information between networks
terms.example: BGP allows your on-premises router and AWS VGW to automatically discover and share routes without manual configuration

terms.definition: An encrypted point-to-point connection between two network endpoints using the IPSec protocol suite
terms.example: Each AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection creates two IPSec tunnels for redundancy

terms.definition: A horizontally scaled, redundant VPC component that allows bidirectional communication between VPC resources and the internet
terms.example: Your public subnet's route table points 0.0.0.0/0 to the Internet Gateway for internet access

terms.definition: A set of rules (routes) that determine where network traffic from a subnet or gateway is directed
terms.example: Private subnet route table: 10.0.0.0/16 → local, 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway

terms.definition: A shared data center where multiple organizations house their servers and networking equipment, often where Direct Connect locations are hosted
terms.example: An organization places their router in an Equinix colocation facility that has a Direct Connect location, enabling a physical cross-connect to AWS

terms.definition: A networking connection between two VPCs that enables them to route traffic privately within the AWS network using private IP addresses
terms.example: Connecting a development VPC and a shared services VPC so developers can access shared tools without going over the internet

terms.definition: A design approach that ensures a system remains operational even when individual components fail
terms.example: Deploying one NAT Gateway per AZ ensures that if one AZ's NAT Gateway fails, other AZs continue working normally
